# `silk/time/zoned`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Instants seen in a time zone: the [`ZonedDateTime`](#ZonedDateTime) type, and [`ZonedText`](#ZonedText) for its RFC 9557
text such as `2026-11-19T15:36:22-03:00[America/Sao_Paulo]`.

## When to use

Use a [`ZonedDateTime`](#ZonedDateTime) when a point in time must keep the place it belongs to: a meeting, a
departure, a time shown to a person. It gives the local date and time, and it finds the
instant of a local time with the daylight saving rules of the zone. For a point in time
without a place, use `Instant`. For a date and time on no timeline, use `PlainDateTime`.

## Details

A `ZonedDateTime` is an `Instant` and a borrowed `Zone`, so it is `Copy`, and it cannot
outlive the zone. Get the zone from the `TimeZones` service of `silk.time.zones`.

To read text, first parse it with [`ZonedText.parse`](#ZonedText.impl.parse), which needs no zone. Then load the
zone that the text names, and call [`ZonedDateTime.fromText`](#ZonedDateTime.impl.fromText). The two steps are separate
because loading a zone is an effect and parsing is not.

## Errors

- `TimeParseError` from [`ZonedText.parse`](#ZonedText.impl.parse).
- `LocalTimeError` from [`ZonedDateTime.fromLocal`](#ZonedDateTime.impl.fromLocal) and [`ZonedDateTime.fromText`](#ZonedDateTime.impl.fromText).

## Examples

### Show an instant in a zone, and read a local time

```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.plain_date_time { PlainDateTime }
import silk.time.zone { Disambiguation, LocalTimeError, Zone, ZoneDataError }
import silk.time.zoned { ZonedDateTime }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let rome = run Zone.fromPosixRule("CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3")
  let seen = ZonedDateTime.make(Instant.fromUnixSeconds(1795109782), &rome)
  if seen.time().hour() != 18 || seen.offset().totalSeconds() != 3600 {
    return 1
  }
  let noon = PlainDateTime.fromFields(2027, 7, 1, 12, 0, 0)
  match ZonedDateTime.fromLocal(noon, &rome, Disambiguation.Compatible) {
    Result<ZonedDateTime, LocalTimeError>.Success { value } => {
      // Summer time is two hours ahead of UTC.
      if value.instant().toUtc().time().hour() != 10 {
        return 2
      }
    }
    Result<ZonedDateTime, LocalTimeError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 3
    }
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 9
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

## `OffsetConflict`

```silk
pub enum OffsetConflict
```

What [`ZonedDateTime.fromText`](#ZonedDateTime.impl.fromText) does when a text states a UTC offset that its zone does not
have at that local time, which happens when the rules of a zone change after the text was
written.

<a id="OffsetConflict.Use"></a>

### `Use`

```silk
Use
```

Keep the instant that the offset in the text gives. The local time can change.

<a id="OffsetConflict.Ignore"></a>

### `Ignore`

```silk
Ignore
```

Do not read the offset. Keep the local time and find the instant in the zone.

<a id="OffsetConflict.Prefer"></a>

### `Prefer`

```silk
Prefer
```

Use the offset if the zone has it at that local time. If not, keep the local time and find
the instant in the zone.

<a id="OffsetConflict.Reject"></a>

### `Reject`

```silk
Reject
```

Fail with `LocalTimeError.OffsetMismatch` if the zone does not have the offset at that
local time.

<a id="ZonedDateTime"></a>

## `ZonedDateTime`

```silk
pub struct ZonedDateTime<'z>
```

An instant seen in a time zone.

### Details

The value is an `Instant`, a borrowed `Zone`, and the UTC offset of the zone at that instant.
`==` is true for the same instant in zones with the same name. `+` and `-` with a `Duration`
move along the timeline, and trap when the result is outside the range of `Instant`. `-`
between two values gives the `Duration` between their instants. `Display` writes RFC 9557
text such as `2026-11-19T15:36:22-03:00[America/Sao_Paulo]`.

<a id="ZonedDateTime.impl.fromLocal"></a>

### Associated function `fromLocal`

```silk
pub fn fromLocal(
    local: PlainDateTime,
    zone: &'z Zone,
    choice: Disambiguation
  ) -> Result<ZonedDateTime<'z>, LocalTimeError>
```

Returns the instant at which a clock in `zone` shows the date and time `local`, and uses
`choice` when the time does not name exactly one instant.

#### Errors

- `LocalTimeError.Skipped` or `LocalTimeError.Repeated` if `choice` is
  `Disambiguation.Reject` and the time names no instant or two.
- `LocalTimeError.OutOfRange` if the instant is outside the range of `Instant`.

<a id="ZonedDateTime.impl.fromText"></a>

### Associated function `fromText`

```silk
pub fn fromText(
    text: &ZonedText<'_>,
    zone: &'z Zone,
    conflict: OffsetConflict,
    choice: Disambiguation
  ) -> Result<ZonedDateTime<'z>, LocalTimeError>
```

Returns the value that the parsed text `text` names in `zone`.

#### Details

`zone` must be the zone that [`ZonedText.zoneName`](#ZonedText.impl.zoneName) names; this function does not compare
the names. A text with `Z` gives that instant. A text with a numeric offset is read as
`conflict` says. An offset without seconds also matches a zone offset that rounds to it,
because the text of a `ZonedDateTime` rounds its offset to the minute. A text without an
offset gives the local time, with `choice` for a time that does not name exactly one
instant. A text without a time gives the start of the day.

#### Errors

- `LocalTimeError.OffsetMismatch` if `conflict` is `OffsetConflict.Reject` and the zone does
  not have the offset of the text at that local time.
- `LocalTimeError.Skipped` or `LocalTimeError.Repeated` if `choice` is
  `Disambiguation.Reject` and the local time names no instant or two.
- `LocalTimeError.OutOfRange` if the instant is outside the range of `Instant`.

<a id="ZonedDateTime.impl.startOfDay"></a>

### Method `startOfDay`

```silk
pub fn startOfDay(self: Self) -> Option<ZonedDateTime<'z>>
```

Returns the first instant of this local day in the zone, or `None` if it is outside the
range of `Instant`.

#### Details

This is midnight on most days. On a day when clocks go forward over midnight, the day
starts when the clock shows a later time.

<a id="ZonedDateTime.impl.checkedAdd"></a>

### Method `checkedAdd`

```silk
pub fn checkedAdd(self: Self, span: Duration) -> Option<ZonedDateTime<'z>>
```

Returns the value `span` later on the timeline, or earlier for a negative span, or `None`
when it is outside the range of `Instant`.

#### Details

The span is exact elapsed time. Across a change of offset, the local time moves by a
different amount: one hour after 01:30 on a day when clocks go forward at 02:00 is 03:30.

<a id="ZonedDateTime.impl.checkedSubtract"></a>

### Method `checkedSubtract`

```silk
pub fn checkedSubtract(self: Self, span: Duration) -> Option<ZonedDateTime<'z>>
```

Returns the value `span` earlier on the timeline, or later for a negative span, or `None`
when it is outside the range of `Instant`.

<a id="ZonedDateTime.impl.write"></a>

### Method `write`

```silk
pub fn write(self: Self, output: &mut [u8], at: usize) -> usize
```

Writes the value as RFC 9557 text, as in `2026-11-19T15:36:22-03:00[America/Sao_Paulo]`,
at `output[at]`, and returns the offset after it.

#### Details

The offset is rounded to the minute, as ECMAScript Temporal writes it. The text has a
fraction, without zeros at the end, when the nanosecond part is not zero. It is at most 40
bytes plus the length of the zone name.

#### Gotchas

Traps if `output` is too short.

## `ZonedText`

```silk
pub struct ZonedText<'text>
```

The parts of RFC 9557 text such as `2026-11-19T15:36:22-03:00[America/Sao_Paulo]`, read
without a zone. [`ZonedDateTime.fromText`](#ZonedDateTime.impl.fromText) turns it into a value.

### Details

The value borrows the text for the name of the zone.

<a id="ZonedText.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string<'text>) -> Result<ZonedText<'text>, TimeParseError>
```

Reads the parts of RFC 9557 text such as `2026-11-19T15:36:22-03:00[America/Sao_Paulo]`.

#### Details

The text is a date, optionally a time, optionally `Z` or a numeric offset after the time,
and a time zone annotation in brackets. The annotation is required. Its content is not
checked against any list of zones. More annotations can follow, as for the other parsers.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.MissingZone` if the text has no time zone annotation.
- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedCharacter` if the name of the zone has a byte that is not an
  ASCII letter, a digit, or one of `/`, `_`, `-`, `+`, `.`, and `:`.
- The other reasons, as for `PlainDateTime.parse`.
